title: Frontier Exploration with Learned Occupancy Maps
abstract: We study how a mobile robot chooses frontiers to visit while building an occupancy grid, and show that a learned map prior shortens exploration paths.

sections.title: 1 Introduction
sections.text:
Exploration asks a robot to cover an unknown building quickly.

Frontiers are the boundary between known free space and unknown space.

sections.title: 2 Method
sections.text:
The planner scores each frontier by information gain divided by travel cost. A convolutional network predicts the occupancy of unseen cells, which sharpens the gain estimate.

The zebrafish module is only mentioned here so that a search for it has one right answer.

sections.title: 3 Results
sections.text: Across forty simulated floor plans the learned prior reduced path length by eleven percent.
